title: “You are my war club, my weapon for battle—
paragraphs:
“You are my war club, my weapon for battle—
with you I shatter nations,
with you I destroy kingdoms.”
— Jeremiah 51:20 (NIV)
Listen.

This isn’t just about war.
This is about purpose.
God was speaking of using a nation as His instrument—His tool of judgment. But here’s where it cuts deeper…

You want power.
You want influence.
You want to matter.
But the real question is—
Whose hands are you in?
Because even a weapon in the wrong hands destroys the wrong things.
And here’s the tension…

We were once weapons of sin.
Sharp with pride.
Loaded with anger.
Aimed at people instead of darkness.
But then—
Jesus stepped in.

He didn’t discard you.
He didn’t melt you down.
He redeemed you.

The cross wasn’t just forgiveness.
It was reassignment.

From weapon of destruction
to instrument of righteousness.
“Offer yourselves to God… as weapons of righteousness.” (Romans 6:13)
So now—

You don’t fight people.
You fight for souls.

You don’t destroy lives.
You help restore them.

That tongue? Now it speaks life.
Those hands? Now they lift the broken.
That story? Now it points to Jesus.
But here’s what we miss…
A weapon only works when it surrenders to the hand that wields it.
So surrender again.
Let God aim your life.

Because in His hands,
you don’t bring chaos—
you bring Kingdom.
